linkedin.hook: Formal verification for Blend v2 b-tokens changes how we handle leveraged collateral on Soroban.
linkedin.copy:
Composable leverage usually breaks at the accounting layer. In pooled lending models, undercollateralized positions drag down solvencies across the entire protocol during liquidity crunches. When architecting Vanna SmartAccounts, our team isolated debt obligations at the individual account level while allowing native ingestion of formally verified Blend v2 b-tokens.

Performance on Soroban is heavily tied to state read throughput and event ingestion. By relying on ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, our smart contracts evaluate collateral ratios in near real time. Liquidations trigger strictly at a 1.10x Health Factor floor, removing the need for defensive over-collateralization buffers that usually kill capital efficiency.

Coupled with average execution costs near 0.00014 XLM fixed gas, Soroban now supports high-frequency deleveraging loops that were previously cost-prohibitive on EVM networks. Institutional risk teams and builders can inspect our b-token integrations and deploy an isolated sandbox directly at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Technical breakdown: How we ingest Blend v2 b-tokens into Vanna SmartAccounts for isolated leverage on Soroban
reddit.copy:
Most leverage protocols on alternative VMs run into two main roadblocks: gas spikes that turn liquidation loops unprofitable, and pooled risk architectures where one bad asset threatens the entire contract state. When we started building Vanna on Soroban, the goal was simple: bring modular leverage to Stellar without those structural trade-offs.

### The Architecture: SmartAccounts and Blend v2

Blend v2 relies on b-tokens, which represent yield-bearing supply positions in isolated or shared pools. Instead of pooling deposited collateral into a monolithic vault, Vanna deploys an isolated SmartAccount sandbox for every user.

When you deposit b-tokens into your Vanna SmartAccount, the contract takes custody of the yield asset, locks it inside your instance, and borrows target assets against it based on strict pool parameters. Because the accounting is siloed inside your account state, bad debt in one position cannot cascade into other users' balances.

### Execution and Risk Numbers

We spent months tuning the risk parameters for Soroban runtime constraints:

1. Fixed Gas Overhead: Base contract calls execute at approximately 0.00014 XLM fixed gas. This lets users run small position adjustments and continuous compounding without fees eating the net APR.

2. Latency Pipeline: We run against Mercury indexers with an average latency of ~320ms. This prevents stale liquidation triggers and ensures position health reflects real-time pool conditions on Blend.

3. Liquidation Boundary: The Health Factor floor is set at 1.10x. Because execution is cheap and state updates land fast, positions do not require excessive collateral padding to remain safe during high volatility.

### Testnet Deployment

You can inspect the contracts and spin up a SmartAccount directly on testnet. Connect your wallet, grab test tokens, deposit b-tokens from Blend v2, and test automated leverage loops.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol. We are actively collecting feedback on contract boundaries, edge cases in b-token math, and liquidation mechanics on Soroban.
